# Locality Guide: Funchal, Madeira, Portugal (1830-1910)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** City status since 1514; capital of the Madeira Islands, settled 1424 (Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funchal).
- **County seat / administrative center:** Funchal, divided into parishes (freguesias) including Sé, Santa Maria Maior, São Pedro, São Martinho, São Gonçalo, Monte, Santa Luzia, and Santo António.
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Madeira Islands, Portugal.
- **Population during period:** not available from the place_population tool for this survey (query returned 'Place not found'); Wikipedia gives a modern population of ~105,795-112,000, not period-specific.
- **Religious denominations:** Overwhelmingly Roman Catholic; also a British/Anglican expatriate community (wine trade) with its own chaplaincy and registers in Funchal.
- **Key historical events:** British wine merchants settled from the 17th century; Funchal was the administrative/ecclesiastical center for the whole archipelago during this period.

## Boundary changes
No boundary changes to Funchal itself are indicated by the records surveyed. Funchal city has long been subdivided into multiple parishes (freguesias), each of which generated its OWN baptism/marriage/death register series — this is a parish-level split within one stable municipality, not a jurisdictional boundary change.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date / level:** Civil registration (Registros civis) in Portugal began in 1832 for non-Catholics (national level), became universal in 1878 with priests acting as civil registrars for Catholics, and became fully obligatory with priests removed from that role in 1911 (FamilySearch Wiki, Madeira Islands Genealogy: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Madeira_Islands,_Portugal_Genealogy). For MADEIRA specifically, priests continued as civil registrars through 1911 — later than the mainland transition — so almost the entire 1830-1910 target window for Antonio Fernandes Lucas is covered by CHURCH, not civil, registers.
- **What exists:** Civil registration records proper begin at the national/municipal level; for Madeira the practical equivalent for 1830-1910 is the Catholic parish register.
- **Where held:** Conservatória do Registo Civil de Funchal (two addresses given on the FamilySearch Wiki Funchal page) for civil-era records; municipal level, moving to district office after 100 years.
- **Gaps:** No 19th-century civil registration series distinct from church registers was found for Funchal in this survey.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Roman Catholic (parishes above); also a small Anglican/British chaplaincy community.
- **Record types:** Batismos (baptisms), Casamentos (marriages), Óbitos (deaths/burials), plus Processos de Casamento (pre-nuptial marriage proceedings) and Dispensação (marriage dispensations, held at diocesan archives, mostly undigitized) (FamilySearch Wiki, Portugal Church Records: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Portugal_Church_Records).
- **Where held:** Original registers at the Arquivo Regional e Biblioteca Pública da Madeira (ARM) in Funchal; images for several Funchal parishes are on FamilySearch as browsable (catalog entries olib:3400414 Monte, olib:3400415 civil registros, olib:3400416 Santa Luzia [fully detailed below], olib:3400417 Santa Maria Maior, olib:3400418 Santo António, olib:3400419 São Gonçalo, olib:3400420 São Martinho, olib:3400421 São Pedro, olib:3400423 Sé).
- **Santa Luzia parish detail (as a model of what the series looks like; catalog hit olib:3400416):** Casamentos (marriage) volumes run PT-ARM-PFUN03-2-160 (1681-1774), -161 (1774-1797), -162 (1797-1810), -164 (1828-1845), -165 (1845-1857), -1239 (1857-1859), then annual volumes 1886-1911 (-1526 through -6505). Batismos run from 1680 through 1911 in similarly numbered volumes. The Santo António parish register (olib:3400418) was found in the Catalog but not hydrated with its own volume list in this survey — the researcher should pull its filmNotes directly.
- **Gaps:** The Santo António parish's own volume inventory was not retrieved in this pass (catalog hit returned un-hydrated); a follow-up catalog_search with hydration targeted at that single hit is needed before assuming coverage dates.
- **Language:** Portuguese (Anglican register content noted as English for the British chaplaincy volumes).

### Civil/parish combined collection
- FamilySearch: **Portugal, Madeira, Catholic Church Records, 1044-1990** (collection 4426199; index & images; 17,724,441 persons) — primary FamilySearch collection for Madeiran baptisms, marriages, deaths across this period.
- FamilySearch: **Portugal Baptisms, 1570-1910** (1520601), **Portugal Marriages, 1670-1910** (1520605), **Portugal Deaths, 1640-1910** (1520606) — nationwide indexes (index only, no images) that include Madeiran localities; useful as a secondary/cross-check index.
- FamilySearch: **Portugal, Civil Records, 1437-2023** (4474701) — index & images, 33,916,026 persons, spans into the civil-registration era.
- MyHeritage ($): Portugal, Madeira, Index of Baptisms, 1738-1910; Portugal, Madeira, Index of Marriages, 1574-1940.
- Arquivo Regional da Madeira (ABM) online: Baptisms 1860-1911 (incomplete for all parishes) and Marriages "early to 1911" (stated by the FamilySearch Wiki Madeira Islands Genealogy page to include all marriages for the entire archipelago) — https://abm.madeira.gov.pt/pesquisa/casamento/.
- Tombo.pt: Portugal, Madeira, Civil Registration Records — free, browsable images, incomplete for all localities — https://tombo.pt/en/d/madeira.

### Probate and court records
- Wills (Testamentos) exist per the general Portugal Church Records pattern but no Madeira-specific probate collection was returned by collections_search or catalog_search in this survey; treat as held at ARM/district archive pending confirmation.

### Immigration/emigration records
- FamilySearch Catalog: **Portugal, Madeira, Funchal, registros de imigração** (multiple parts, e.g. olib:3714413 covering 1846-1878), at ARM; online per catalog listing.
- Passport applications: Applications for Passport volumes for Funchal 1851-1863 appear in volume_search (imageGroupNumbers 008038197_001/002/003), 0% name-indexed but full-text searchable.
- FamilySearch collection: Portugal Passport Registers and Application Files, 1800-1946 (1925427, index only).

### Other record types
- British/Anglican chaplaincy records: Parish registers of the Church of England in Portugal, Anglican Chaplaincy (Funchal, Madeira), 1848-1851 — baptisms and burials for British subjects, catalog hit koha:155172, microfilm 574493; related index koha:603804 (christenings 1848-1851, extracted in English).

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Gap it fills | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Portugal, Madeira, Catholic Church Records 1044-1990 (4426199); Portugal Baptisms/Marriages/Deaths indexes; parish-level browsable image sets for each Funchal freguesia | Primary index+image source for Madeiran church records | Free |
| Arquivo Regional da Madeira (ABM) | Baptisms 1860-1911 (incomplete); Marriages early-1911 (archipelago-wide) | ABM's own online search by name, directly from the original custodian | Free, https://abm.madeira.gov.pt/pesquisa/casamento/ |
| Tombo.pt | Portugal, Madeira, Civil Registration, Catholic Church Records, and Passports | Browsable images including some not on FamilySearch | Free, https://tombo.pt/en/d/madeira |
| MyHeritage | Portugal, Madeira, Index of Baptisms 1738-1910; Index of Marriages 1574-1940 | Alternate index of the same ARM material | Subscription |
| Ancestry | Portugal Select Marriages 1670-1910; Portugal, Madeira Passports 1872-1910 | Alternate index access | Subscription |

**Coverage of this survey:** volume_search matched 22,003 volumes for this place/period; only the first 10 were detailed above (a mix of passport, religious marriage, and baptism volumes), and the summary count of volumes by record-type group could not be computed (request to the FamilySearch group-service timed out) — treat the record-type volume counts as unknown, not zero. catalog_search returned 59 total hits; 25 were examined, 10 hydrated with full detail.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Arquivo Regional e Biblioteca Pública da Madeira (ARM), Funchal | Original parish registers for all Funchal freguesias, ARM reference codes PT-ARM-PFUN0x-... | In-person, or via ABM's online database/catalog |
| Conservatória do Registo Civil de Funchal | Civil registration post-1911 (and any earlier civil-only acts) | In-person / mail; two listed addresses on the FamilySearch Wiki Funchal page |
| Funchal Portugal FamilySearch Center | Access to digitized/microfilmed holdings | In-person, Rua Tenente Coronel Sarmento 25, Funchal |

## Records NOT online
- Marriage dispensations (Dispensação), held at diocesan archives, are stated by the FamilySearch Wiki Portugal Church Records page to be mostly undigitized.
- The Santo António parish's own ARM volume list (image group numbers / date spans) was not retrieved in this survey (catalog hit olib:3400418 not hydrated) — its existence is confirmed by the Catalog, but specific volumes and dates are not yet in hand.

## Known record losses
No record loss specific to Funchal or Madeira was stated by any tool result in this survey. The general transfer of Portuguese parish vital records to the state in 1910 is noted by the FamilySearch Wiki (Portugal Church Records, Madeira Islands Genealogy) as having resulted in some records being lost nationally during that transfer, but no Madeira-specific loss was named.

## Research tips
- Civil registrars did not take over from priests in Madeira until 1911 (later than the mainland's 1878 date) — search the Catholic parish register, not a civil office, for a c.1838 birth and any pre-1911 marriage (FamilySearch Wiki, Madeira Islands Genealogy: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Madeira_Islands,_Portugal_Genealogy).
- Couples usually married in the bride's parish (FamilySearch Wiki, Portugal Church Records: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Portugal_Church_Records) — if Antonio Fernandes Lucas married a second time, check neighboring Funchal freguesias (Sé, Santa Maria Maior, São Pedro, São Martinho, São Gonçalo, Monte, Santa Luzia) as well as Santo António, since the bride may have been from a different parish.
- After the mid-1800s, Catholic marriage records typically add marital status, parents' names and residences for both bride and groom — useful for distinguishing a same-named man in multiple marriage entries (FamilySearch Wiki, Portugal Church Records).
- Use ARM's own name-search database (https://abm.madeira.gov.pt/pesquisa/casamento/) alongside FamilySearch's browsable images, since ARM's marriage index is stated to cover the whole archipelago to 1911, while FamilySearch's parish-level images must be browsed by freguesia and year.
- Women in Portugal traditionally retained their maiden surname; adoption of a husband's surname became briefly common only in the late 19th century, fading again by century's end (FamilySearch Wiki, Portugal Naming Customs) — do not expect a wife to appear under her husband's surname in later records.

entry.narrative_markdown:
## Question

Whom did Antonio Fernandes Lucas (born about 1838-1839, Santo António, Funchal, Madeira; son of José Fernandes Lucas and Francisca Luisa) marry, other than Maria Joana (married 8 February 1890)?

## Conclusion

The evidence indicates that Antonio Fernandes Lucas married once only, to Maria Joanna de Jesus on 8 February 1890, and that he was a bachelor at that marriage. No earlier or additional marriage of this man was found. The 1859 marriage of an Antonio Fernandes Lucas to Antonia de Jesus belongs to a different man of the same name. Tier: probable.

## Evidence

**1. The subject's own marriage entry states he was single.** The Santo António parish register for 8 February 1890 records the marriage of Antonio Fernandes Lucas, aged 51, and Maria Joanna de Jesus, aged 21, "ambos solteiros" (both single), the groom being the legitimate son of José Fernandes Lucas and Francisca Luiza, both deceased. The priest recorded that they came with all papers in order and "sem impedimento algum canonico ou civil", and the groom signed the entry. This was read from the original register image, not only the index. It is original, primary information on marital status (the party himself presented it and signed), direct evidence that no earlier wife existed. Citation: "Portugal, Madeira, Registros da Igreja Católica, 1044-1990", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:6BG7-FC2X : Wed Jul 16 09:44:56 UTC 2025), Entry for Antonio Fernandes Lucas and Maria Joanna de Jesus, 8 de fevereiro de 1890. The parents named match the tree parents (José Fernandes Lucas, Francisca Luisa), so the entry is the subject's.

**2. The apparent earlier marriage is a namesake's.** On 20 July 1859 at Santo António an Antonio Fernandes Lucas married Antonia de Jesus (daughter of José Marques and Joanna Felicia). His stated parents are Manoel Fernandes Lucas and Luiza de Jesus, not José Fernandes Lucas and Francisca Luisa, so he is a different man. The record-linking score against the subject is about 0.0000014. Citation: "Portugal, Madeira, Registros da Igreja Católica, 1044-1990", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:6BG7-MQ3D : Wed Jul 16 08:21:21 UTC 2025), Entry for Antonio Fernandes Lucas and Manoel Fernandes Lucas, 20 de julho de 1859. The information about parentage is secondary (given by the parties about their parents) but it is internally consistent and is contradicted by nothing. The couple's two daughters named Maria, who died aged two on 30 May 1889 and aged one on 5 September 1894, name this Antonio and Antonia de Jesus as parents; those entries are tied to the namesake, not to the subject, and the second death (1894) postdates the subject's 1890 marriage while the subject's own family was then being raised with Maria Joanna, which is consistent with two separate households.

**3. Family-cluster records show no earlier wife.** The 31 July 1871 burial of José Fernandes Lucas (aged 74, wife recorded as Francisca Lucas, informant not present, official register) names no daughter-in-law. The 20 August 1896 baptism of the subject's son Antonio, a primary record with the parent as presenter, names the father Antonio Fernandes Lucas and mother Maria Joanna de Nobrega, with no hint of a previous wife. The mother's surname appears as de Jesus in 1890 and de Nobrega in 1896; her parents (Antonio de Nobrega, Luiza de Jesus) are the same in both entries, so this is the same woman. (Two relationship assertions in the 1896 entry also attach her parents to the father's persona; this is an extraction artifact, not a claim, and is disregarded.)

## Conflicts and limits

No conflict is registered. The only apparent contradiction, the 1859 marriage, is accounted for above by differing parentage. The conclusion rests on one original statement of bachelorhood plus a negative search: no marriage or burial of a wife naming this Antonio's parents was found in Funchal parish registers for 1858-1911. Negative evidence is weaker than a positive record. A marriage in an unindexed register or under a bride's home parish (couples usually married in the bride's parish) could have escaped the index, although the 1890 bachelor statement makes a pre-1890 marriage unlikely, and a widower after 1890 would still have to appear in the searched 1890-1911 window. The unreached sources (Arquivo Regional da Madeira marriage index, diocesan pre-nuptial proceedings, Tombo.pt image mirror, MyHeritage index) would corroborate rather than narrow the answer. Because research is not exhausted and the finding is partly negative, the tier is probable, not proved.

## Tier

Probable. Stated as a conclusion that no marriage other than that to Maria Joanna de Jesus is recorded for this man, pending the unsearched alternate indexes named above.

---

Antonio Fernandes Lucas, born about 1838 in the Santo António parish of Funchal, most likely married only once, to Maria Joana on 8 February 1890. His own marriage entry, read from the original church register, says both he and his bride were single, so he had no earlier wife. The other Antonio Fernandes Lucas who married Antonia de Jesus in 1859 was a different man, since his parents had different names. The two daughters named Maria who died young belong to that other man and his wife. Records for Antonio's father and for his own children show no sign of a prior wife. A few further indexes and church files were not searched: the Madeira regional archive's marriage index, the diocese's pre-wedding files, MyHeritage's indexes, an image mirror site, and the pending FamilySearch hints on Antonio.

---

**Research is finished.** Both parts of the objective are answered at tier *probable*:

- **Wife named Antonia de Jesus?** No — the man who married Antonia de Jesus in 1859 was a confirmed namesake (parents Manoel Fernandes Lucas and Luiza de Jesus, same_person score of 0.0000014 against GK89-82B). Antonio's own 1890 marriage record states he was a bachelor (*solteiro*).
- **Daughter named Maria who died young?** No — the daughters Maria who died in 1889 and 1894 belong to that same namesake family, not to GK89-82B.
